summary: Second-order linear equation. 3 methods apply: Undetermined coefficients, Variation of parameters and Laplace transform.

methods.name: Characteristic equation
methods.reason: On its own this only solves the homogeneous equation (right-hand side 0). It is the first stage of the other methods here.

methods.name: Undetermined coefficients
methods.reason: The coefficients are constant and the right-hand side \(e^{x}\) is made of polynomials, exponentials, sines or cosines.

steps.title: Write the characteristic equation
steps.text: For constant coefficients, try \(y = e^{rx}\). Substituting and dividing by \(e^{rx}\) leaves a quadratic in \(r\).

steps.title: Solve for the roots
steps.text: The discriminant is positive, so there are two different real roots. Each gives an exponential solution.

steps.title: Homogeneous solution
steps.text: This solves the equation with the right-hand side replaced by 0.

steps.title: Guess the particular solution
steps.text: Guess a combination of the right-hand side's terms and all of their derivatives, with unknown coefficients.

steps.title: Substitute and match coefficients
steps.text: Put \(y_p\) into the equation and compare the coefficient of each kind of term on the two sides.

steps.title: Write the general solution
steps.text: Add the homogeneous and particular solutions.

steps.title: Apply the initial conditions
steps.text: Substitute \(x = 0\) into \(y\) and \(y'\), set them equal to \(1\) and \(0\), and solve the two equations for \(C_1\) and \(C_2\).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets both initial conditions.

methods.verify_note: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets both initial conditions.

methods.name: Variation of parameters
methods.reason: It works for any right-hand side once the homogeneous equation is solved, at the cost of two integrals.

steps.title: Write the characteristic equation
steps.text: For constant coefficients, try \(y = e^{rx}\). Substituting and dividing by \(e^{rx}\) leaves a quadratic in \(r\).

steps.title: Solve for the roots
steps.text: The discriminant is positive, so there are two different real roots. Each gives an exponential solution.

steps.title: Homogeneous solution
steps.text: This gives the two solutions \(y_1\) and \(y_2\) the method builds on.

steps.title: Compute the Wronskian
steps.text: The Wronskian of \(y_1\) and \(y_2\) is \(y_1 y_2' - y_2 y_1'\).

steps.title: Set up the parameters
steps.text: Look for \(y_p = u_1 y_1 + u_2 y_2\) with \(u_1' = -\dfrac{y_2 f}{W}\) and \(u_2' = \dfrac{y_1 f}{W}\).

steps.title: Integrate
steps.text: Integrate each one. No constants are needed here; they are already in the homogeneous solution.

substeps.title: Integral for u1: substitution
substeps.text: Let \(u\) be the inner expression; its derivative appears in the integrand.

substeps.title: Integral for u2: substitution
substeps.text: Let \(u\) be the inner expression; its derivative appears in the integrand.

steps.title: Particular solution
steps.text: Form \(y_p = u_1 y_1 + u_2 y_2\) and simplify.

steps.title: Write the general solution
steps.text: Add the homogeneous and particular solutions.

steps.title: Apply the initial conditions
steps.text: Substitute \(x = 0\) into \(y\) and \(y'\), set them equal to \(1\) and \(0\), and solve the two equations for \(C_1\) and \(C_2\).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets both initial conditions.

methods.verify_note: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets both initial conditions.

methods.name: Cauchy–Euler (y = x^r)
methods.reason: The equation does not have the form \(ax^2 y'' + bx y' + c y = 0\).

methods.name: Reduction of order
methods.reason: The characteristic-equation methods already give both solutions here.

methods.name: Laplace transform
methods.reason: The equation is linear with constant coefficients and the initial conditions are given at 0.

steps.title: Transform both sides
steps.text: Take the Laplace transform of each term, writing \(Y(s) = \mathcal{L}\{y\}\). Derivatives turn into multiplication by \(s\), with the initial values appearing.

steps.title: Insert the initial values
steps.text: Replace \(y(0)\) and \(y'(0)\) with the given numbers and collect the \(Y\) terms.

steps.title: Solve for Y(s)
steps.text: This is now an algebra problem.

steps.title: Split into partial fractions
steps.text: Break \(Y(s)\) into pieces that each appear in a table of Laplace transforms.

steps.title: Transform back
steps.text: Take the inverse transform of each piece. The result is the solution for \(x \ge 0\).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets both initial conditions.

methods.verify_note: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets both initial conditions.

methods.name: Series solution
methods.reason: With constant coefficients the other methods give the exact solution, so a series is not needed.
